location_qualifier: northeastern corner of the pocket; headquarters place not named
source_locator: R566: p. 358, 359; R169: text and table of 1945
current_activity: Gruppe von Lüttwitz, two corps under one headquarters, holds the north face of the Ruhr pocket near Lippstadt
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 16 p. 358: "brigaded under Luettwitz's headquarters as Gruppe von Luettwitz"; p. 359: "turning the northeastern corner short of Lippstadt, some twenty miles up the Lippe from Hamm, Gruppe von Luettwitz". Event definition: the perimeter as it stood when the pocket closed on 1 April. Event support: one source family (CMH); the Lexikon lists an Armee-Abteilung von Lüttwitz under Army Group B in April 1945 without a place. Location: Lippstadt, North Rhine-Westphalia with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: Lippstadt stands for the northeastern corner of the group front; no headquarters place is named. Location support: CMH puts the group in the north and turning the northeastern corner short of Lippstadt. Commander: Generalleutnant Heinrich Freiherr von Lüttwitz. Opponents: US Ninth Army. Context: CMH calls the command Gruppe von Luettwitz; the project unit GER-AA-LUETTW (Armee-Abteilung von Lüttwitz in the Lexikon) is taken to be the same command, and the unit note says it was formed by combining two corps under the headquarters of the XLVII Panzer Corps.

location_qualifier: representative point inside the pocket; the surrender place is not named
current_activity: Gruppe von Lüttwitz ends in the Ruhr pocket by 18 April, when all resistance stopped; no single day is given
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 16 p. 370: "Bayerlein of the LIII Corps, Luettwitz of the XLVII Panzer Corps, Waldenburg of the 116th Panzer Division, Denkert of the 3d Panzer Grenadier, Lange of the 183d Volks Grenadier, commanders of the 180th, 190th, and 338th Infantry Divisions, and the final remnants of the 9th Panzer Division"; p. 372: "On 18 April all but a few stragglers gave up, all resistance at an end". Event definition: CMH lists the unit among the prisoner-of-war commanders after the rush of 16 April without a day for it, so the date is the end of resistance on 18 April and is approximate. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Ruhr pocket (representative point at Essen) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a representative point at Essen for the Ruhr pocket; the surrender place is not named. Location support: CMH names no place for the surrender. Commander: Generalleutnant Heinrich Freiherr von Lüttwitz. Opponents: US First and Ninth Armies. Context: CMH p. 358 says the group was two corps under the headquarters of Luettwitz's XLVII Panzer Corps; the capture of Luettwitz on p. 370 stands for the end of the group, and CMH gives no separate date for it.
